content.text:
## Final report

**Best design: 3 mm graphite (single layer), evaluated 3rd (candidate b-0002).**

My own assessment against the limits from `brief` (the tool computes none of this):

| Requirement | Limit | 3mm graphite value | Margin | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 screen | ≤420 K | 401 K | 19 K | pass |
| R2 FE hotspot | ≤340 K | [331.37, 331.37] K | ~8.6 K | pass |
| R3 areal mass | ≤100 kg/m² | 5.4 kg/m² | 94.6 kg/m² | pass |
| R4 thickness | ≤40 mm | 3 mm | 37 mm | pass |

All four requirements pass with real margin. This beats every design in the prior constellation on mass — the lightest prior pass was 10mm graphite at 18 kg/m², vs 5.4 kg/m² here — while still clearing the FE hotspot limit comfortably.

Evaluation trail: 1mm graphite (b-0000) failed R2 outright at 344.4K; 5mm (b-0004) passed at 327.8K; 3mm (b-0002) also passed at 331.4K and is lighter, so it's the best I found within my 3-evaluation budget.

**With more budget** I'd bisect between 1mm (fail, 344.4K) and 3mm (pass, 331.4K) — try 2mm next. The trend (344.4→331.4→327.8K as thickness goes 1→3→5mm) suggests 2mm might land close to 337-338K, which would still pass but with a much thinner margin, so it would need direct FE confirmation rather than extrapolation before trusting it.
